problem:
$$
{y}^{″}+8y=f(x),\,y(0)=-2,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0
$$

Consider the initial value problem above, where $f(x)$ is an even, $2\pi $-periodic function. Select the missing part in the solution of the IVP, where the second infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution of the differential equation.

$$
y(x)∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$
worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of a linear differential equation of the form ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(x)$ is given by $y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p},$ where ${y}_{c}$ is the solution to the homogeneous equation and ${y}_{p}$ is a particular solution.

First, we address the particular solution ${y}_{p}.$ Since $f(x)$ is an even function and the differential operator contains no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits the symmetry and is also an even function consisting only of cosine terms. This is represented by the term

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Next, we find the homogeneous solution. The characteristic equation ${\lambda }^{2}+8=0$ gives roots $\lambda =\pm \sqrt{8}\text{i}.$ So, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{8}x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{8}x).
$$

To find the unknown constants, we apply the initial conditions. Differentiating the total solution gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)∼-A\sqrt{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{8}x)+B\sqrt{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{8}x)-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

Using the derivative condition ${y}^{′}(0)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & =-A\sqrt{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+B\sqrt{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\ 0 & =0+B\sqrt{8}-0 \\ B & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Note that because the total solution is an even function, its derivative is an odd function, which must vanish at $x=0.$

Next, we use the condition $y(0)=-2.$ With $B=0,$ the total solution is

$$
y(x)∼A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{8}x)+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Applying $y(0)=-2$ and noting that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =A+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n} \\ A & =-2-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $A$ back into ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{8}x),$ we find the missing part:

$$
y(x)∼\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{8}x)(-2-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n})+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$
